Series::is_cuda¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

bool Series::is_cuda() const noexcept

What It Does¶

Returns true when this Series currently lives on the CUDA platform, false otherwise (CPU, or a different accelerator such as MPS).

It is a metadata read — platform() == Platform::CUDA — that never transfers data, never probes the machine, and cannot throw.

is_cuda() is the strict, per-backend test. It sits below is_gpu: every CUDA Series is also is_gpu(), but a Series on MPS is is_gpu() and not is_cuda(). Reach for is_cuda() specifically when the work you do next depends on the CUDA backend being the one in play — a CUDA-only kernel path, a cudaStream-aware call, a transfer policy that only makes sense for CUDA. When the branch is “accelerator vs. CPU” and the backend identity does not matter, is_gpu is the right predicate.

As with all the platform predicates, is_cuda() reports where this tensor is. Whether the machine can run CUDA at all is pluss::platform_available(pluss::pCUDA) — a different question, answered before you decide to move data there.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

bool true iff platform() == Platform::CUDA.

Gradient¶

Not applicable — is_cuda() returns a plain bool.

Examples¶

Example 1. On a host without CUDA, is_cuda() is false for every Series — including accelerator tensors on a different backend. (Output from an Apple-Silicon host: MPS available, CUDA not.)

auto x = pluss::series::zeros({2});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "cpu tensor: is_cuda=" << x.is_cuda() << " is_gpu=" << x.is_gpu() << "\n";
if (pluss::platform_available(pluss::pMPS)) {
  auto m = x.to(pluss::pMPS);
  std::cout << "mps tensor: is_cuda=" << m.is_cuda()
            << " is_gpu=" << m.is_gpu()
            << " is_mps=" << m.is_mps() << "\n";
}

Output¶

cpu tensor: is_cuda=false is_gpu=false
mps tensor: is_cuda=false is_gpu=true is_mps=true

The MPS tensor is on an accelerator (is_gpu() == true) but it is emphatically not CUDA — is_cuda() pins the exact backend where is_gpu() only says “off CPU”.

Example 2. is_cuda() (this tensor) vs pluss::platform_available(pluss::pCUDA) (this machine).

auto x = pluss::series::zeros({2});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "x.is_cuda()                        = " << x.is_cuda() << "\n"
          << "platform_available(pCUDA) [machine] = " << pluss::platform_available(pluss::pCUDA) << "\n";

Output¶

x.is_cuda()                        = false
platform_available(pCUDA) [machine] = false

On a CUDA host the second line reads true and you may then call x.to(pluss::pCUDA); afterward is_cuda() on the moved tensor reads true. The two lines answer independent questions — “is the backend here” and “is this tensor on it”.

Example 3. is_cuda() is noexcept and metadata-only — content, dtype, and shape never affect it, and it is free to call in a hot loop.

auto x = pluss::make_series({std::nan(""), 1.0, 2.0});
std::cout << "is_cuda=" << std::boolalpha << x.is_cuda()
          << "  (unaffected by the NaN, the shape, or anything but placement)\n";

Output¶

is_cuda=false  (unaffected by the NaN, the shape, or anything but placement)

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • is_cuda() is strict: an accelerator Series on MPS is not is_cuda(). Use is_gpu for “on any accelerator”.

  • It reports this tensor’s placement, not the machine’s capability. Use pluss::platform_available(pluss::pCUDA) before deciding to move data to CUDA.

  • A binary op requires both operands on the same platform; a CUDA tensor and a CPU tensor cannot be combined directly (move one with to()).

  • The predicate never transfers data and never throws.

Summary¶

is_cuda() reports whether a Series currently resides on the CUDA platform:

  • strict per-backend: platform() == Platform::CUDA

  • a subset of is_gpu — every CUDA tensor is is_gpu(), not vice versa

  • distinct from pluss::platform_available(pCUDA) (a machine capability)

  • noexcept, metadata-only

See Also¶

  • Series::is_gpu: “on any accelerator” — the backend-agnostic branch.

  • Series::is_mps: the other strict per-backend test.

  • Series::is_cpu: the exact complement of is_gpu().

  • Series::platform(): the underlying Platform value (cpu / cuda / mps).

  • Series::to: move a Series onto (or off) CUDA.
